Add duckctl quack

`robotctl quack` over the radio: `duckctl --name duck-d041 quack` plays
that robot's chirp, and since every voice is seeded from the SoC
serial, the duck that answers is the one the name reached.

btd routed `robot.sound` to a refusal "until a client wants it"; this is
the client, so the call now reaches robotd. The theremin, chorale and
flashlight stay refused.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5
limp fall is on by default

Merge pull request #380 from pollen-robotics/duckctl-quack

Add duckctl quack

[roller]: the roller's own networks and stick speeds

The roller robot gets a section of its own in robotd.toml, and so in
`robotctl configure`:

  walk     roller locomotion          unset = roller.onnx
  stand    standing at zero command   unset = none
  crouch   the B-button crouch        unset = roller_crouch.onnx
  vx_max / vx_min / vyaw_max / vyaw_min   the pad's speeds on wheels

On wheels those three networks take the place of [policy]'s walk, stand
and ground_pick, which are now the walking robot's alone, so trying a
roller network can no longer write over the walking one. A slot loaded or
reset while rolling (`robotctl policy load`, robot.loadPolicy) is written
to [roller]. A roller stand, when named, is selected at zero command as
walking's is; with none (the default) the roller network runs at every
velocity, as before.

The speeds were constants in padd (push 0.6, brake 0.5, yaw 0.3 rad/s);
they are the defaults now, re-read live like [pad_drive]. The networks
ride the [policy] reload.

docs: the pad over UDP — udp-pad.md owns it

The page owns turning it on, the wire format and the sender's rules; the spec's wire table
becomes a link. restart-order.md names netpadd in the install and skew lists. robotctl configure
now maps [netpad] to a restart of both netpadd and padd, which the registry-completeness test
had been failing on since the keys were added.

pad-map: a dropout spends the hold in flight, fired or not

A button still down when the pad came back was timed from the
reconnection, so Start held across a Wi-Fi gap stood the robot up on
release, and Select rested it. HoldButton::reset now always marks the
hold spent; it clears on the first tick that reads the button up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

padd.service: ask --should-run only of a release that ships netpadd

A rollback skips postinstall, so the new unit stays while current points
at an older padd without the flag; clap exits 2, systemd skips, and the
rollback leaves the robot with no pad and no failure. A release without
netpadd has no selector, so padd simply runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

udp-pad.md: an example that drives, and what the robot really does

The Python sender paused 1.5 s between packets, so each was the first
after a silence and fired nothing. It now streams at 30 Hz from a still
pad, taps Start twice, walks, sends one stale datagram, and falls
silent — checked against netpadd and a fake robotd. Also: both units
can be briefly active after a one-sided restart, and a restarted sender
is picked up within timeout_ms rather than at once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

robotctl pad status: an inactive padd under [netpad] enabled stood down

It advised `systemctl start padd` on a robot where the UDP pad has the
robot. robotctl reads [netpad] enabled from the config it already knows
(unreadable counts as off, as for padd) and says padd stands down for
netpadd, pointing at udp-pad.md. No proto change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

duckctl udp-pad: say why nothing is happening, once per change

A refused send was silently ignored, and a missing pad said nothing, so
a duck without [netpad] enabled looked like a sender that worked. Each
is now one line per transition: nothing listening (with the likely
cause), any other send failure, recovery, and the pad found or gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

netpadd: the silence test fails if serve has died

A serve that returned also sends nothing, so the test passed for the
wrong reason. It now keeps the handle and asserts serve is alive on both
sides of the silence.

Merge origin/main into udp-pad

padd took two changes on main while it was being split into pad-map: the robot sitting down
when a driving pad drops out (#372), and the Home button toggling the flashlight (#375). Both
land in the split shape. The pad-loss state machine and the reading of the robot's answers move
to pad_map::loss so netpadd can share them; Home is pad_map::Buttons bit 12, which was reserved
on the wire and is now the middle button.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

netpadd: a client gone sits the robot, as a lost Bluetooth pad does

When the UDP client goes quiet — the pad unplugged from the laptop, the program stopped, the
network gone — the robot now does what padd does for a Bluetooth pad that drops out: it asks
where the pad went, sits a second later if it is standing, and greets the client when it comes
back. robotd's idle look-around runs meanwhile, as for any still robot.

Also spends any hold on Accept::Connected, so the first client after netpadd starts (every
update, every robotctl configure) cannot stand the robot up by letting go of a Start it was
already holding. duckctl udp-pad sends Home.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

robotd: play emotions as skills (robot.do sad)

An emotion is two files in [emotions] dir (default /var/lib/robot/emotions): <name>.json, the
keyframes in the microduck_emotions format, and <name>.wav. robot.do <name> plays it, so it goes
on a pad button like any skill (robotctl pad bind y sad), from every client, with no new call.

While one plays, the loop puts its frame in place of the clients' head, body pose and mouth, with
a zero twist, for that tick: the same policy and safety as the sticks, and the clients' values
back when it ends. Started only on a robot the policy drives with no move in flight; a fall,
limp-fall, Start or a rest ends it and cuts its sound. "skill": "sit" sits the robot down.

The names are listed wherever robot.do's are (the refusal, pad bindings, the subscribe answer
robotctl pad bind checks). scripts/duck-sim reads them from ~/.cache/duck-sim/emotions. Docs: an
Emotions section in the cheat sheet, a row in robotd-design 4.5.
